newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Israel to stick to Hebron framework.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Israel to stick to Hebron framework.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reaffirmed on Monday he intends to carry out an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron in the framework of peace deals with the PLO.

But in a speech to parliament, the right-wing Israeli leader again gave no timetable for the long-delayed partial pullout or any details of security adjustments he said must be made to protect 400 Jewish settlers in the city of 100,000 Palestinians.
Israeli and PLO negotiators reconvened in Gaza to discuss Hebron and the partial pullout agreed by Israel's previous Labour-led government.

"In the framework of the understandings of the agreement, we are working -- as is our right -- to achieve the requested arrangements to anchor security and to have redeployment in Hebron in more secure conditions," Netanyahu said.

"We are preparing to implement the redeployment in Hebron while guarding two basic principles: securing the lives, existence and security of residents of the Jewish commmunity in Hebron...(and) protecting our holy places in Hebron," he said.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher ended on Monday a two-day visit to Israel and Gaza by saying that "Israel does not intend to try to rescind or modify" the Hebron accord.

The negotiations were the main outcome of an emergency Arab-Israeli summit which U.S. President Bill Clinton convened at the White House last week after a wave of Israeli-Palestinian violence killed 59 Arabs and 15 Jews.
